business_problem: Santander is moving from large general-purpose models toward smaller models specialized for banking tasks, seeking to identify the best model for each workload while maintaining performance and reducing serving costs.
solution_summary: Through Santander AI Lab, the bank evaluates open-weight models against banking tasks in its internally built Model Arena, then specializes models for targeted workloads with NVIDIA NeMo Customizer. For structured-data banking workloads, Santander uses NVIDIA Kumo models to develop predictive intelligence for agentic services. Inference is being industrialized within Santander's own architecture using NVIDIA Dynamo-Triton; the article attributes serving-cost reductions to this approach. Model Arena is also being developed to design, simulate, evaluate, and supervise banking agents, alongside performance engineering and adversarial testing in controlled environments before successful capabilities scale across the bank. The source identifies structured banking data and banking/customer-service tasks, but does not specify ingestion mechanisms, storage systems, deployment topology, or particular downstream application integrations.
